I was fortunate enough to see Josephine at the 62nd Chicago International Film Festival, and it’s quickly becoming one of my favorite films of the year. The film explores collective trauma, female rage, the justice system, and so much more.

It’s bound to enter the 2027 awards season conversation. Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan, and Mason Reeves are all giving top-tier performances. It’s definitely one of Tatum’s best performances. It is a crime if voters overlook Josephine for buzzier films, but either way, it’s worth seeking out.

It’s one of the most thought-provoking works of fiction of 2026 and will haunt you long after it ends.

Josephine works best with minimal knowledge of the plot. Therefore, I will try not to spoil any major storylines. At its core, the film portrays society and how it often scars and fails women and girls.

Josephine follows Josephine (Mason Reeves) as an everyday activity turns into a living nightmare for her and her family. The film isn’t a horror movie, but it often feels that way. The main villain inflicts the level of trauma you expect from some of the great horror movie franchise villains. It leaves you with even bigger scars than these movies, because Josephine’s evildoer is very much grounded in real-life monsters.

The film immediately grips you and takes you into this world by starting with Josephine and her father, Damien (Channing Tatum), bonding and getting ready for the day. You’re automatically invested in this family. The intimacy of the family unit, mixed with the reality of situations like this, makes the movie authentic and heartbreaking.

Many films touch upon difficult subjects. However, not many of them create an atmosphere as well as Josephine. You feel the weight of everything. The subject matter has been done a lot, and sometimes in ways that sensationalize an event to the point of losing the horror in it. Josephine treats the subject matter with care. We need films like this, especially given some of the recent headlines.

It’s a movie that many may connect with, for one reason or another. That’s what makes it timeless because too many stories like the ones depicted in Josephine happen all the time.

The film also works because it tackles some of the emotional and mental toll of trauma, and how that can lead to depression, anxiety, fear, and rage. Josephine is another really thoughtful film about depression and how it can creep into life, even with someone as young as Josephine.

Many of the best courtroom dramas often end with a sense of justice being served. Whether Josephine ends with a positive result or a negative result, it doesn’t matter. It ends with a sense that nothing is completely resolved. That feels more realistic than movies with an impressive lawyer who saves the day.

Real cases often aren’t neatly wrapped up, and justice isn’t always served. However, Josephine’s ending inspires a sense of hope. It shows how resilient the main character is, and women in general. The power is in the ability to persevere even in the darkest times.

Josephine hit the 2026 movie schedule on November 20.

#3746. Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

#3745. Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises."

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever."

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft says the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft announced in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

Amanda Seyfried busted onto the Hollywood scene on soaps in the Noughties, but it was her role in Mean Girls in 2005 that made her a household name. Since then, she’s been in a ton of huge movie and TV roles including Les Miserablès, The Dropout, Big Love, Jennifer’s Body, Dear John, Mamma Mia! and The Housemaid. Not one of these roles led her to landing on the list of celebrity names to ever host SNL. That is, until You Can See Everything came around.

By now, you should at least vaguely know the twist in the Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder doc involves Amanda Seyfried. WhileYou Can See Everything is my favorite film I’ve seen all year (so far), I didn’t think that’s what it would take to get Lorne Michaels to see the light on Seyfried, but it did. Over the weekend, we learned the actress will host Saturday Night Live for the first time EVER in 2026. It’s awesome for her, and I love that she celebrated with a sweet post.

I mean "sweet" in the literal sense. While we know Seyfried can be funny (it’s like she has ESPN or something), she does seem a little nervous about taking the stage at Studio 8h, and asked her fans and pals to “send cake.”

If you are a fan of the actress, you may already know she’s a noted cake lover. She turned 40 during The Housemaid’s promotional tour, and there were so many viral cake moments, including one where she pretty much murdered a cake with a knife. Yes, it was fittingly on brand.

Getting a cake on your birthday is kind of fun, but cake actually has a special place in the actress' heart. She talked about this love of cake with Harper’s Bazaar once, so it’s a real thing.

I pay a lot attention to what I eat, but I don't have any specific slimming method. I eat organic food, a lot of fish, no meat, and I force myself to limit sugar, even if I like it a lot. It takes a lot of effort! I have to practice sport a lot because I love cakes.

I’m genuinely excited for Amanda Seyfried to expand her abilities and to give the late night series a whirl. It's a special rite of passage for a lot of Hollywood, and hey, if she's good, maybe one day she'll even enter the coveted Five Timers Club! Regardless, if you told me all this would have happened because of a literal documentary, I'm not sure I would have believed you.

#3742. Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

"BIS is not a good thing for a game that's supposed to be about role-playing."

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different."

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list."

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

It's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

#3741. GTA 6 Has An Impressive Number Of Accessibility Options To Make The Game Less Frustrating

With Grand Theft Auto 6 casting such a wide cultural net, a lot of people of varying levels of video game experience and skill are going to be playing it, some of whom maybe just want to sightsee or experience the story, and they may find a lot of the friction frustrating. Those people might quickly find themselves on the verge of giving up, but luckily, there are accessibility options built into the game that can be used right from the start.

Accessibility options are different from cheats, in that they donât require you to beat the game or perform specific tasks to unlock them. Theyâre there for people who, for whatever reason, arenât able to make progress with the game when playing the game with its standard difficulty, mechanics, or controls. Be warned that messing with some of these options can significantly alter the balance, and thus your enjoyment, of the game.

Also, unlike cheats, accessibility options do not disable trophies or achievements, nor do they prevent you from saving.

At any point in the game, access the pause menu and scroll all the way down to settings.

Select that option and press RB or R1 to reach the Gameplay section.

From here, scroll down to the bottom under âAccessibilityâ to see multiple options. The ones youâll probably most want to pay attention to are those for Simplified Mini Games, Auto Drive, Accessible Combat, and Reduced Vehicle Damage.

Activating “Simplified Mini Games” makes activities like exercising, hotwiring vehicles, and shooting hoops easier and not so reliant on timing or easing off the analog triggers.Â

Auto Drive is an option with its own sub-options, allowing you to have the game drive for you in leisurely situations like getting to a mission or, if you set it to Unrestricted, use it even when youâre being pursued or chasing enemies. The menu warns that the driving AI may still crash into objects or other cars, so itâs not like a free pass for everything to go perfectly.

The two big ones, Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage, get their own warnings: The game was not built with this in mind. That means you can turn them on, but things will become significantly easier. If you activate these options without needing them, you may start getting bored playing GTA 6.

Accessible Combat reduces enemy health and also damage done to the player, so youâll hurt them more and they will hurt you less. Reduced Vehicle Damage means your car wonât suffer too much in collisions or shootouts, so a T-Bone or two wonât render your car inoperable.

There are other accessibility options that make certain things like boosting while driving a little friendlier. If you ever have a problem controlling something in the game, itâs worth checking to see if thereâs an accessibility option that would change how it works a little bit. Whatever helps you get through the game!

As reported by The Shanghai Observer and Automaton, authorities in Shanghai have arrested 13 people and seized an untold number of unauthorized model kits and figures based on pop culture properties like Final Fantasy. The cops were reportedly put on the trail by a suspect Tifa Lockheart figurine.

Police in Fengxian, a district of Shanghai, began receiving complaints in June. The Shanghai Observer showed pictures comparing a Play Arts Kai (Square Enix's premium figure line) Tifa with a seemingly less articulated counterpart in the same outfit. Reading through machine translation, it sounds like customers in the area bought these figures online expecting the genuine article.

The leader of the operation reportedly commissioned a Guangzhou factory to produce the false Tifa and her ilk. They even sold some figures at higher prices than the genuine article, offering added accessories or features not available in the official product.

I'm of two minds about this, personally: I'm generally pro-kitbashing, selling custom figures, and using proxies in trading card games. In the face of some seriously inflated pricing from official merch lines, bootlegs can often be more enticing than the real deal, particularly if they offer features you can't get from official products⁠—the added customization options from this arrested vendor actually sound weirdly pro-consumer.

But it certainly appears, at least from The Shanghai Observer's reporting, that these suspect figures were being presented as the genuine article to customers. Paired with the increased price vs. official merch, and I find myself soured on the whole operation. It may seem small and silly, but as we endure the Golden Age of Scams, it's weirdly nice to see scammers face some consequences somewhere.

Though it might be sacrilegious to my fellow gay pop girlies, Iâm pretty lukewarm on Carly Rae Jepsen overall, but I will never deny that she has some bops. âRun Away With Me,â the anthemic opener to her 2015 album Emotion, is one of the best pop songs of the century, and I will say that 10 toes down with my full chest. It’s not difficult to imagine why Jennifer Lopez went viral when turned up to the 2000 Grammys in her green dress with a super low-plunging neckline. (That dress looked like it was made for her!) But did you know that The X-Files and David Duchovny also played a role in why it’s such a moment, too? I sure didn’t!

Most people know that JLo’s green Versace “jungle dress” is such a big celebrity fashion moment that it led to the creation of Google Images. It caused such a high volume of online interest that Google, which was only two years old at the time, decided it was time to engineer the feature. Although The X-Files of it all? I had no idea. Lopez told the story of the dress recently, saying this about it:

I was nominated that night and I wore it to The Grammys, and I was very excited. It was just one of those moments… [I didn’t know it was going to be something], I just picked the best dress on the rack.

JLo didn’t set out to create some internet-shattering moment when she stepped out at the Grammys. She just wanted to look good. As she added on Friends Keep Secrets:

When I walked out on stage you could see it on my face because there was like swell in the room of [applause]. And, I was just like, ‘What’s happening?’ And then, David Duchovny was with me, and he was like, ‘This is the first time in years I know nobody’s looking at me.’

So Lopez presented an award with David Duchovny, who was one of the biggest names in TV at the time, who was in his seventh season of the show. In the clip she talked about how at the time Duchovny couldn’t go anywhere without being recognized and had recently filed a multi-million dollar lawsuit against 20th Century Fox. Here they are together:

I can imagine Duchovny feeling perhaps like the heavily covered lawsuit might be the elephant in the room when he was going to The Grammys that night. However, when he was paired with JLo on the night of the green dress, all eyes were on her. As JLo continued:

The thing is I walked out on stage and it was like a bodysuit, right? And it had the material, very just flowy material, like chiffon. And when I walked out, it blew open. The moment was the thing. The wind blew, the people started, he had the perfect line. It wasn’t scripted.

It sounds like the room absolutely lost it when JLo hit the stage with Duchovny, and his line complimented it all like a cherry on top. Even though the moment happened over twenty-five years ago, it has remained relevant over the years with a number of pop culture moments. The most recent one has to be when Mika Abdalla wore the dress during a scene in Off Campus. (The show’s costume designer shouted out how the dress stayed on if you’re as curious as I was).

And then, Rachel Zoe also put on the dress for a magazine cover shoot, too. Last year, the original model who first wore the Versace piece on the runway, Amber Valletta, also slipped back into the chiffon dress. Will JLo ever top this look? We don’t know, but you can see her in The JLO Show, streaming with a Paramount+ subscription on November 26.

Implementing sex into GTA 6 in a believable way was quite tricky to pull off, according to developer Rockstar Games.

This being both a Grand Theft Auto game and a love story, it's not a shocker that sex and intimacy (and the most nudity I've ever seen in a video game) are so prominent in GTA 6. Getting the balance just right was pretty tough, however.

"Exploring the physical relationship between Jason and Lucia required a lot of thought and iteration," Rockstar's vice president of animation, Mark Tennant, explains in quotes given to GamesRadar ahead of our GTA 6 review.

"We needed to allow players to interact with the partner in a natural, loving way, with a believable progression based on their overall investment in the relationship," he adds. GTA 6's romance isn't a totally linear line. Jason and Lucia can be hotly passionate about each other or just be cordial partners in crime, depending on your choices, so how they interact physically needed to match their relationship status.

"This required us to create animation performances that found a realistic balance between player agency and partner response while keeping things fun, passionate, and rewarding," Tennant says.

It's a far cry from how many of the other games in the series dealt with sex, where your main interactions with romantic partners were impersonal and often transactional. On the flip side, GTA 6 is almost always making you consider someone outside of yourself and sex isn't just an awkward animation that plays if you drop some in-game cash. Jason and Lucia's central romance is the reason why Rockstar isn't letting you hire prostitutes this time around, too.

#3733. Total War: Warhammer 40,000 breaks the game into star system mini-campaigns, each with their own stories and objectives

"We want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy."

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do."

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that."

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

Track down this white off-roader for Moses.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The BF Bandito is one of the many cars in GTA 6 that Moses asks you to steal and bring to him for cold, hard cash. This one has a search area out in Buskin Swamp, but when you arrive it's not immediately clear where or how to steal the car.

The owner of this white offroad racer will drive around the map marked search area in a circle, as shown in the clip above. To get him to stop, simply park your car blocking the track and stand next to it. When he reaches you, he'll slow down and call out, at which point you should press L2 to focus on him and use the "Mislead" dialogue option to ask for help.

In my version, Lucia was wearing a ski-mask and had a baseball bat, which quickly convinced them all to run away (after a few swings), but either way, once he stops it's easy to steal the car. The baseball bat probably wasn't necessary, but hey, it's still non-lethal.

As you exit the swamp, you'll get shot at and pursued by a few of his friends, but the BF Bandito is fast enough to outrun them easily. Bring it back to Moses to get $3,400ish as reward, though this may vary based on condition.

#3731. I Thought Rocky And Creed's Big Fight Scene Would Be The End Of I Play Rocky. So What Happened?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Spoilers for I Play Rocky are ahead! You can catch the movie in theaters now.

When I think about the best sports movies, often the big match or game at the center of it comes to mind immediately. For instance, with Rocky, the titular character’s fight with Apollo Creed is something I instantly picture when the film gets brought up. So, I was surprised to see the fight wasn’t really featured within the story of I Play Rocky, the project on the 2026 movie schedule about the making of Rocky. Instead, it was used during the credits.

It turns out there is a reason why that big match was cut from the film and moved into the credits.

Now, even though they took a “week” to film the fight between Rocky and Creed for this movie, it was eventually cut…kind of. Ultimately, the scene was moved to the credits. So, why did that happen? Well, director Peter Farrelly told me the match was actually supposed to be the end of I Play Rocky. However, a big realization about the stairs scene changed his mind, as he recalled during an interview with CinemaBlend:

And by the way, it wasn't originally supposed to be over the end credits. It was supposed to be the end of the movie. But when you get in an editing room, as good as the script is, you have to let the movie find its way. And when he goes up the top of those stairs [and raises his arms up], there was such a high watching it that you couldn't get there again.

While the director was very open about this being the right call with me, he also admitted that it took him a while to fully accept that. It took a long time to film the fight, and it’s such an iconic moment from Rocky. However, he eventually came to the conclusion that they had to move it to the credits:

Like even though we took a lot of time making that fight and doing it, you will never get that high again. You're not going to feel it. And so I showed it to a few people in the editing room. They go, ‘You should end on the top of the stairs.’ I was like, ‘No, I took a week. I took a week to shoot the fight. I'm not cutting the fight.’ And it took me a couple weeks to finally realize I have to cut the fight. It's got to end on the stairs.

I know I was a bit shocked not to see the fight prominently featured in the movie, when so many of the other scenes are. However, I did think it was a cool surprise to cut it into the credits, and it served as a full-circle moment to the scene where we watch Anthony Ippolito’s Sylvester Stallone and Stephan James’ Carl Weathers train for the fight.

Speaking of Ippolito and James, they, like Stallone and Weathers, trained and learned how to box for this movie. That means they took a few punches too. When I asked the Sly actor about filming the fight between Rocky and Creed, he said:

We took some real we took some real shots during that. Me and Stephan were just trying to figure it out, and you know, sometimes we messed up here and there, and we tag each other, but it was all right.

James also confirmed that they took some hits while preparing for and filming this movie. He revealed that he and Ippolito trained together as well, and “got close in a very short period of time,” noting that they were “in the trenches with each other.” That became very clear too, as he told me:

I may have taken a punch or two that I wasn't looking forward to. But you know, had to do what I had to do to pull it off. And I think it was all worth it that we were able to, you know, not only step into these guys psychologically, but physically as well.

Well, considering the amount of time, effort and punches that went into this, I’m happy that Rocky and Creed’s fight did find its way into the movie…even if it wasn’t in the way it was originally intended.

Now, if you’d like to see how this legendary sequence is shown in the credits of the well-reviewed I Play Rocky, you can catch the film in theaters now. And if you’d like to compare their take on the sequence to Rocky’s, you can stream the OG movie with a Paramount+ subscription.

#3730. UK Prime Minister won't be playing GTA 6, government says, while hailing Rockstar Games a "British success story"

Grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

"Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it."

Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

The leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else."

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

#3729. Three Games You Can Play For Free This Weekend On PC

Don’t want to pay $80 for Grand Theft Auto 6? Don’t have a console to play it on? There are alternatives. Here are three games you can play for free on PC this weekned.

Let’s start with Crusader Kings 3. It’s a grand strategy game in which you leverage diplomacy, marriage, personal development, and economic expansion to become a dominant imperial power in the Middle Ages. Whether through statecraft or scheming, you’re basically doing fantasy football for geopolitics while navigating your character’s personal legacy and lore like you might in a visual novel. It’s pretty good! And easy to lose your weekend to. It’s free to play on Steam from now until November 23.

Then there’s Mistfall Hunter. This one is also medieval but decidedly less well-received. It’s a dark fantasy extraction ARPG with both co-op and PvP multiplayer. Unlike most of the extraction games out there, which are shooters, this one is melee-focused. It launched to a 55-percent positive Steam review rating but has been slowly improving. Players have praised the combat and upgrade system despite lots of complaints about balance and server issues. “It be good,” one Steam player wrote today in the review section. “imo its not fun,” wrote another. It’s normally $25 but currently free to play until November 23.

Finally, we have Mark of the Deep, aâwait for itâpirate-themed, isometric soulslike metroidvania. You’re shipwrecked on a magical island searching for your crew while fighting skeletons, monsters, and other dark creatures. It’s gesturing in the direction of games like Death’s Door and Tunic, but sounds like it doesn’t reach the same highs and has been criticized for its arbitrary difficulty and occasional movement bugs. The good news is there’s no stamina bar, so you can dodge-roll to you heart’s content. It’s free to claim from the Epic Games Store until November 26.

There are rows of GTA 6 tanks waiting to be liberated right from the start of the game, to earn the Challenging Tank award

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Getting a tank in GTA 6 represents the pinnacle of criminal behavior, and there's a long history of stealing Rhinos going all the way back through the series to GTA 3! These military vehicles are virtually indestructible so you're safely protected inside, and they pack a powerful enough punch with their cannon to destroy anything GTA 6 puts in front of you. You also need to get inside one to unlock the Challenging Tank Trophy or Achievement, so to help you out with that, here's how to steal a tank in GTA 6.

The location for an entire row of GTA 6 tanks is in the Mile Zero Air Station, situated west of the area you begin the story in, which you can reach by driving through Abismo Key and on to Southwind. You'll need a vehicle to break into the military base which will get left behind, so it's best not to use your GTA 6 personal vehicle for this job, and equipping body armor from Ammu-nation is highly recommended for added protection.

By following the route marked on my map above you'll weave through several road barriers, as which point the soldiers will open fire on you, then turn right at the first opportunity to pass more barriers and soldiers until you spot a handy pile of dirt. You must use this Stunt Jump to clear the perimeter fence, though if you don't get enough height to also clear the inner fence you can smash through it to reach the runway.

Look to your left when on the miliary runway and you'll see a large building, and to the left of that are the Rhino tanks we're looking for – you can also head to the right of that building if you'd prefer to grab a GTA 6 jet instead. Once you reach the tanks, crash through the fence and then approach one before using the usual enter vehicle button to climb in through the front hatch. Note that there is various military hardware in this area, but the Rhino tanks are the ones closest to the fence you broke through.

You can then drive away in your new GTA 6 tank, which will shortly unlock the Challenging Tank award from the GTA 6 Trophy and Achievement list to add to your collection. Strangely, commandeering this military vehicle doesn't initially increase your GTA 6 Wanted Level beyond the existing two-stars for breaking into the base, though this soon goes to five and then six-stars when you start blasting things with your cannon.

Don't expect to get too far in your Rhino tank, as it drives pretty slowly and you're being constantly peppered with incoming gunfire plus rockets from helicopters – which you can shoot down if you aim your barrel high enough. However, the tank will eventually run out of fuel or become so damaged that it is completely incapacitated, and as surrender is no longer an option the upcoming Wasted is unavoidable.

The Wanted Level you get won't affect your current GTA 6 criminal profile, though you can only get a six-star Wanted level in GTA 6 if you go all in on a psychotic rampage!

#3727. 8 Amazing Indie Games We Think You Should Go Play

Indie GamesQueen's DomainSonic Pico ParkTanuki: Pon's SummerWell Dweller

I’m seeing reports that some folks have already blazed through GTA 6‘s story, finishing the game roughly 48-ish hours (depending on your time zone) after its release. And of course, there are those gamers who don’t plan on playing the game at all, untouched by the powerfully seductive force of GTA 6 FOMO. Whatever your reason for having a free gaming calendar right now, I’ve come bearing gifts with which you can fill it. I’ve sampled my Kotaku colleagues as well as conducted my own research to assemble a smattering of recently released indie games you can play right now.

Dig Dig Dino was originally released on the Playdate before coming to Steam this week. It’s from the developers of the well-liked western action game Arco, though this time they’ve gone for something much smaller, simpler, and cuter. In Dig Dig Dino you play as an paleontology intern tasked with using your shovel and a growing arsenal of tools to find dinosaur bones. You start with limited stamina, only able to dig so much in a day. But as you chew through layers of dirt and sedimentary rock, you pick up treasure that gets exchanged for cash with which you can buy more more stamina, upgrades for your tools, and new tools like a dog who will sniff out bones for you.

The game sounds almost too simplistic to be any kind of fun, but I found myself spending hours digging, hoping the next run would reveal the final piece to my saurian puzzle. There are different dig sites that require different tools and yield different treasures, but don’t expect to discover the kinds of finds that would excite the dearly departed Dr. Alan Grant. The dinos you discover in this game are weird, and though I’m only a few hours (and a few competed skeletons) in, I suspect there’s a greater mystery about the world to discover as you dig deeper.

Sonic Pico Park may have the blue blur in the name, but itâs developed by the small team at TECOPARK, which created the original Pico Park. The cooperative puzzler lends some Sonic the Hedgehog flair toÂ Pico Park‘s cooperative, ragebait puzzle platforming action. The game is a lot of chaotic fun in which up to eight players will yell at one another, then lock in to solve some difficult challenges. Work on your team-building skills as Sonic, Shadow, and several other characters from across the series. Lone wolves need not apply; youâve gotta play with folks you can still like after youâve been tied to one another and tried to coordinate running through a loop-de-loop. â Kenneth Shepard

Maybe you’re a big fan of Dark Souls, Elden Ring, or even King’s Field. Maybe you’re craving that next Elder Scrolls. Or maybe you’re just not super interested in cars and guns and want something a bit more medieval. Friends, let’s pay a visit to Queen’s Domain, a gorgeous first-person RPG in classic-PlayStation style that combines a very clonky, retro-feeling combat and exploration system with much more smoothness to movement and menuing than the games that inspired it could ever muster. Queen’s Domain has you exploring a mysterious island full of magic and monsters in search of your father. You’re puny and weak when you start, enemies hit hard and sneak up on you, and for the most part the game tells you very little about how to proceed: you just have to experiment and pray. But that’s exactly what some people (like me) want, and the feeling when something finally clicks is exhilirating. I hear there’s a pretty big twist midway through that blows the game wide open, too, though I haven’t experienced it yet for myself. â Rebekah Valentine

Tanuki: Ponâs Summer is one part Tony Hawk, one part mail delivery game, and one part cozy slice-of-life sim. Also, you play as an adorable Tanuki who waddles around the open-world village and forest that make up the game’s map. Iâve had a lot of fun pulling off sick tricks while delivering packages to locals and learning more about them. Sometimes, these moments lead to mini-games in which you help out the villagers with sumo wrestling, running a bar, or chopping down trees. But mostly, you spend a lot of time doing tricks on a BMX bike in a gorgeous little world that Iâve been having a great time poking at between big GTA 6 sessions. â Zack Zwiezen

Wanderburg is a bullet heaven action-roguelike in which you play as a medieval fortress on wheels swerving around the countryside as armies collide and new territories are conquered. Itâs sort of like Vampire Survivors if it starred the castle from Howlâs Moving Castle. Itâs also similar to TerraTech Legion, another vehicular spin on the auto-shooter genre, except with some Age of Empires flavor mixed in. Itâs in Early Access on Steam right now and itâs my go-to run-based arcade shooter for the fall. – Ethan Gach

CRACK is a type of game that’s not usually my bag. Itâs an incremental co-op comedy adventure, not something Iâd usually touch, but my son loves these types of games and so I spent more time with it than I expected to. You live in a mysterious lab with a giant egg in the middle. Your job is to crack pieces of it off and trade them in for money, which you use to get upgrades to get better tools to knock off better chunks of the egg and, well, you can see where this is going. But the egg is alive, and the more you chip away the angrier it gets, eventually causing dangerous outbursts that lead to chaotic mayhem. Thatâs the friendslop part of it. Throw in the mystery of the lab itself, with clear influences from games like Portal, and youâve got a surprisingly clever social twist on making the numbers go up. – Ethan Gach

Well Dweller is the fourth metroidvania by Kyle Thompson, and if you donât know who that is, just think Hollow Knight but shorter and more chill. While seemingly influenced by Team Cherryâs aesthetic sensibility and gameplay formula, Thompson has been refining his own take on the genre for several games now. Plus you know what? Silksong came out over a year ago. We could use a spiritual successor or two, and Well Dweller earns its keep as one of the better ones. You play as a bird with a matchstick that can do all sorts of whimsical things, leading to some satisfying traversal and combat, even if itâs not very deep. For those who want a breezier action metroidvania, thatâs a plus. – Ethan Gach

Have you heard the good word of Dressmaker yet? Dressmaker is about exactly what you think it is: you make dresses. But itâs not just a color-swapping dress-up game. No, youâre doing this stitch-by-stitch. Youâre choosing the fabric, picking out adornments, cutting pieces to patterns along the bias, stitching them together, adding the lace trim, all to customer (or your own) specifications. The ridiculous amount of detail that Dressmaker goes into, coupled with an enormous array of dressmaking options that you unlock as you play, already has made it a beloved favorite this year. And some of the dresses people are making are ridiculous! But whether youâre skilled or just throwing together some cloth, Dressmaker is undeniably delightful. – Rebekah Valentine

#3726. Star Wars: Galactic Racer studio "didn't dream" Biddy Blas would be as popular as he is

"He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly."

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has said it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

Since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

"Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!"

Fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose said.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole new level.

"It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly."

Blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who said his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

"You can't help but take it a little bit personally".

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

When Bethesda got its hands on the Fallout licence way back in 2004, the naysayers were many and vocal. In fairness, the naysayers are still many and vocal, but they were back then too, and it turns out Bethesda saw at least a few of their posts. In a chat with The Examined Game, Skyrim lead Bruce Nesmith reflected on the reaction some Fallout old-heads had to Bethesda's acquisition of the series.

"There was huge pushback when Bethesda got the Fallout licence to do Fallout 3. There was a lot of people who were Obsidian fans, who were like 'Bethesda's gonna screw it up, they're just gonna make it Skyrim, we want Fallout the way we remember Fallout', and there was a strong, vocal community that just hated that we were gonna make that game".

For clarity's sake, the angry fans at the time were likely Black Isle and Interplay fans rather than Obsidian fans—the latter studio hadn't ever made a Fallout game in 2004 (though it had Fallout alumni on staff), and they were prophesying (after 2006) that Bethesda's take on Fallout would be like Oblivion, not Skyrim, since the latter released in 2011. I suspect Nesmith is muddling the initial negative reaction with, well, the more modern one, which is shaped in large part by Obsidian's excellent Fallout: New Vegas from 2010.

"We had to prove them wrong", recalls Nesmith, "and fortunately we did, because Fallout 3 was embraced even by a lot of our sceptics". It's true: people bloody loved Fallout 3 and still do, though there are of course still series fans who reject the game. "There's always going to be some diehard people that say 'Fallout 2 was the greatest Fallout game ever', but we tried our best to just not engage… because you're not going to win that argument.

"All you can do is make the best game you can and let that be your statement. And that's what Bethesda did".

Does the vitriol ever get to Bethesda and its devs? Unsurprisingly, yeah, a little. "Any time somebody says that the thing you're doing is, you know, fill in your blank for all the cuss words and the bad things… you feel like it's a statement about yourself. You have to divorce yourself from that [but] you can't help but take it a little bit personally. But it does make you want to prove them wrong. It does make you want to say 'I'm going to show you that this will work, that we can respect the franchise and make it better and make it our way, rather than the old way".

Sometimes a text can cause a lot of drama.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, on the 2026 TV schedule, only just debuted as the first spinoff, and immediately had its own drama. Funnily enough, the biggest drama of the season involved O.G. Mormon Wives star Mayci Neeley, who got dragged into the mix when older sister McCall DaPron clashed with some of the new cast members.

Things quickly escalated when McCall made Mayci aware of some drama with co-star Bobbi Althoff, resulting in a text to Jen Affleck saying, “I’m gonna f*** them up,” in regard to the individuals who clashed with her sister. And then, Jen told everyone what Mayci said. After it all became public, it was suddenly so much bigger than just venting between sisters, making someone who had previously been thought of as one of the most grounded and level-headed of the original Mormon Wives series come across like a mean girl.

I’m sure we’ve all said things in a text in the heat of the moment, but Mayci’s words got out for all to see, leading her to realize her mistake in responding in the heat of the moment. She also expressed real regret for having made the statement at all. In a recent apology statement, she said:

To be honest, I’m embarrassed. I’m genuinely embarrassed that I said that. I don’t remember the intention behind it because I know I wasn’t trying to get into a street fight, like a physical fight. It’s genuinely embarrassing. I don’t know why the hell I said that.

Even though the text did make me look at Mayci a bit differently from the impression I’d gotten of her on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, I also understand wanting to defend a family member and don’t blame her for having a strong reaction to feeling like her sister was being attacked. It all felt a bit middle school, and I’m certainly not making ay excuses for her over-the-top response, but the firsthand experience with some wild drama on her own reality TV series probably led Mayci to have a more heightened reaction than she might otherwise have had.

Anytime you get a group of people together who come from different backgrounds, have them spend long periods of time together, and point cameras at them, you’re bound to get some drama as they get to know each other. It was a bit unusual that this particular drama came from someone not actually in the room where it happened, but it sounds like Mayci has definitely learned a lesson from the fallout. She went on to say:

I am very sorry I said that. I did regret saying that. That is definitely out of character for me. … I’m just going to be accountable for the things that I was upset with myself for. I’ve apologized for it, and moving on.

Largely because of Taylor Frankie Paul, we’ve become accustomed to Mormon Wives being synonymous with drama, especially with the chaos surrounding production of the original series. After the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody issues with her children, and her announced departure, it immediately turned attention to the new spinoff and the drama in the OC. So, I’m glad that Mayci didn’t seem to waste any time in sharing such an honest reaction to her own behavior.

While we don’t yet know the future of this new series, fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt is getting her own reality show. You can check out The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives and its Orange County spinoff with a Hulu subscription while we await news of future seasons, other possible spinoffs, and more headline-making drama.

#3723. GTA 6 players are already pulling off high-flying tricks and other impressive stunts, just days after launch

One of the best things to emerge from Grand Theft Auto over the years has been the community's truly spectacular stunts: players soaring under bridges, leaping across buildings, and more. And with GTA 6's release this week, we've seen the first signs of the trend continuing in a brand-new world.

This TikTok video by user Gstitz from early in GTA 6, for instance, claims to be the "world's first" demonstration of a Mallard flying sideways between a narrow gap in a large building. It takes several attempts, but they eventually pull off the stunt without crashing or broken parts.

Another video from Hazardous is a more grounded (literally) look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and shows the YouTuber flinging motorbikes and cars around the map as they explore promising high-risk jumps. Some of these locations are tied to in-game challenges, so there are certainly breadcrumbs placed by Rockstar to encourage such ventures.

Granted, these are far from the truly absurd stunts we've seen in prior Grand Theft Auto games. But as a firing gun for the wider community, it's a great start. They're also among the most impressive things we've seen in GTA 6's opening week.

It's doubtless been an eventful few days though. Players have been entranced by the slapstick violence and in-game social media. Even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has praised the game, despite not having time to actually play it. Eurogamer editor-in-chief Chris Tapsell also came away impressed, lauding it in his five star GTA 6 review.

If you're playing the game and need some help, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough, and our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheat list.

#3722. How To Solve All Main Puzzles In GTA 6′s Tenebrae Lux

If you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI. While on the surface it looks like just a funny gag poking at auteur culture (and one developer in particular), Tenebrae Lux is a surprisingly solid, short puzzle game that (if you’re not using this guide) may take you a few hours to get through.

But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it quickly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help. I get you. Here’s as simple a walkthrough as I could manage for Tenebrae Lux:

You’ll start out on the shoreline. You can’t do much: just walk around and examine objects. To start with, you’re going to want to head to the left side of the shore (assuming you’re facing the shore from the beach you start on) where there are multiple run-down shacks lit by big bright lights.

Inside these shacks are three puzzles on gridded boards. On those grids, multiple pieces are placed with different 3D shapes atop: three-tiered tall ones, middling spiky ones, and flat ones with a tiny dot in the middle. The flat ones don’t move at all, the middle-sized spiky ones can slide across the board and clear the flat ones if they land next to them, and the three-tiered tall ones and middle-sized ones clear one another in the same fashion. Your goal is to clear all the pieces off the board.

You can do these puzzles in any order. One of them is easy and straightforward, but the other two require a little bit more thinking. You’ll have to use the fact that the flat pieces don’t move and cannot be cleared by the three-tiered pieces to set up the three-tiers so they and the mountain pieces can clear one another once all the flat ones are off the board.

The three main puzzles in this area should be fairly simple to do, though there are a couple of hidden ones you can optionally do that are more difficult. On at least one, you might need to set up your board so you have two three-tier pieces set up with a gap between them that a middle-sized piece can easily get into after clearing a flat one. See below:

When I move that mountain-shaped piece to the left, it will take out itself and all three of those other tiles with it.

This puzzle will easily make you feel like you’re losing your mind, but I highly recommend trying to work it out for yourself first, if you can.

When you enter the room upstairs in the bunker, you enter a loop that will keep perpetuating each time you go through the door and up the stairs. The room will be almost identical each time you enter it, but for two things. The first will be the calendar, which will show the date as being one of six different dates, and the second will be one of the other objects in the room.

Your goal is to find a six-digit code and enter it into the phone, followed by the # sign, to proceed.

In order to get the code, you need to pay attention to what day it is, and what is different in the room on that date. If you keep going up the stairs over and over, the dates will eventually cycle back through, so if you miss one don’t worry, you can keep going to see it again. The dates are as follows: October 11, 14, 20, 23, 27, and 30. You won’t see the dates in any particular order, but you’ll need to put them in that order when you input the numbers for each date into the phone.

The numbers themselves, you get from finding what’s “different” in the room on a given date, and working out what number the difference corresponds to. There are ten possible differences, and your playthrough won’t have all these objects in the roomâit’s random each time, though consistent within a single playthrough of the puzzle. Here are the ten possible differences:

Once you get the code right, exit upwards one last time and on you go.

This one was waaaaay more confusing to me than it needed to be. The goal is to cross the bridge off to the left of the ruins. The bridge has multiple rows of weird symbols on it. You have to walk over the correct symbol in order to proceed. If you walk over the wrong one, a lamp will go out. If you do it wrong three times, you fail and the puzzle resets.

The trick to figuring out the correct symbols is in the ruins and the poem on the plaque just outside.

The ruins will contain the following items, which correspond to the following descriptors in each of the seven lines of the poem:

The items will be scattered across the ruins. Also in the ruins you will find a bunch of weird, esoteric symbols glowing on the ruined archways above. These symbols correspond to the symbols on the bridge.

To solve this, you need to visit each of the items in the order they appear in the poem, and match the item with the symbol on the ruins that corresponds to it, then follow the symbols across the bridge in order (the direction they’re facing doesn’t matter). It can be a bit tricky to figure out which symbol goes with which item. The best way I can describe it is the symbol for each item is the one that’s over the doorway “entrance” to each item, so the one you have to pass under to reach it.

Here’s a map to show you what I mean. Orange circles are places where the objects can appear, and green triangles are where symbols are. I’ve numbered them, but please don’t mistake the numbers for the correctÂ order of the objects: that’s going to be determined by the poem, and the poem’s order is random.

Also note that #1 below is on the ground, because the arch has collapsed.

This can still be confusing, so let me walk you through what I got as an example. Here’s my poem:

First up is moon, which for me was straight ahead through the first door.

Two days of rest says nothing, so we move to the third line, which mentions forests. Here’s the tree:

Third verse mentions gold, then earth, in order. My trophy was past the mark that had crumbled to the ground, and my earth was at the very start of the puzzle:

This next line is a bit tricky, as it mentions both sun and moon. But there are only seven lines on the bridge, and the items are only used one time each. So we just focus on sun here. I didn’t get a good picture of my sundial, sorry!

The last two lines in order mentions fire first, then drinking, which is water. Here’s fire:

So I’d follow those symbols in order across the bridge. It may help to draw a map on a piece of scrap paper or in a notebook for this one so you don’t have to slowly walk back and forth over and over.

If you fail, the puzzle will fully reset itself, and you’ll have to look at a new version of the poem and ruins and try again.

This bit is a little creepy and again confusing at first, but quite easy once you work it out. All you have to do is walk in the door that’s the furthest away from any of the figures walking through the doors.

In the photo above, the man is walking toward the third door from the right, so I want to go to the farthest door on the left.

As you go, more figures will start to appear. When there are multiple, you want to try and split the distance as best as possible. You also have to avoid any doors that say they’re out of order, so if they have a sign on them, go to the next one furthest away from the man. On the last set of doors, there was no way to get away from the men, so I just walked directly between two of them.

Once you pass through the last door, you’ve officially beaten Tenebrae Lux!

#3720. 13 arrested in Shanghai as police crackdown on bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine operation

Chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are currently being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

The investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

The appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

Looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

Deciding whether to proceed or postpone the Protective Custody story mission is a big choice you'll need to make in GTA 6. The mission appears on your map as "Meet Abe" in Chapter 5, once you've completed the mission Operation Savage Glory.

Once you get to Abe's office, Jason will warn Lucia that everything will change after this mission. Lucia will hesitate at the door as you make your choice to "Proceed" or "Postpone."

This is a pretty big decision, because Protective Custody kicks off the final mission of the game which takes about an hour to play. And even though it's a binary choice between "Proceed" (which starts the mission) and "Postpone" (which delays the mission)" there's actually a third possible outcome based on when you make the choice.

It's a long mission that will take about an hour to play, so be prepared. You can't save during this mission so make sure you've got the time! Once you've completed the final mission, you can watch the credits and return to the open world so you can continue playing.

You will go back to the open world to continue playing. The "Meet Abe" icon will remain on your map so you can begin the final mission at any point from then on.

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and I won't spoil them here. But one of the endings is only possible if you postpone the Protective Custody mission until you've deposited $2 million into your Buck Me savings account. That's why when you choose to proceed with the final mission makes a difference.

It's also worth noting (again, without spoilers) that just because you do have $2 million in your Buck Me savings account does not guarantee you will see this particular ending. There are still choices you'll need to make in the final mission that determine which ending you see.

#3718. So Is The $100 GTA 6 Ultimate Edition Actually Worth It?

Before Grand Theft Auto 6 even launched, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics. So, now that GTA 6 is here and I’ve spent over 150 hours with it, I can share what’s in the Ultimate Edition, how you access this stuff, and if it’s worth upgrading from the standard $80 version of GTA 6. The short version is…eh, probably not.

In GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall. These stores include an exclusive tattoo parlor, street clothing shop, and hair salon. Now, at first, I thought it was pretty shitty of Rockstar to hide stores behind a paywall. And to be clear, it still does suck that a few shops are only accessible if you pay $20 more. But after playing GTA 6, I discovered that the world is filled with over 600 stores. There are already so many clothing, car, hair, make-up, and nail options in the base game. So the Ultimate Edition’s extra few stores don’t feel that necessary. And after actually visiting these shops and seeing what they have to offer, I don’t think people are missing out on that much.

First up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear. There’s some alright stuff in here, including some nice-looking jeans for Jason and a cool graphic shirt or two. And a really wild fuzzy hat for Lucia. But the options in here aren’t something you need to have. You can create plenty of great and cool outfits without stopping by this Ultimate Editionâonly retailer.

Next up is the tattoo shop Electric Fang. Of all the Ultimate Edition stores, this is the coolest one to enter. And I do think some of Electric Fang’s tat designs are solid. But again, there are so many other options in the game for ink that I’m not sure these are very necessary or worth the $20 upgrade.

Sara’s Unisex Salon might be the best of the bunch as it offers some stylish hairdos for both Jason and Lucia. But on top of that, it offers some really nice makeup options for Lucia and cool nail art, too. I ended up using some of these options during my time as Lucia because I liked them so much. Still, again, there are so many other good options for haircuts and nail art already in GTA 6 that I’m not sure you need to spend $20 more on this version.

There are also two exclusive car mod garages in GTA 6‘s Ultimate Edition. One of them, Rideout Customs, offers some really gaudy and exotic paint and accessories options. If you wanted a neon-pink car with stripes painted to look like cheetah print, well, this is the place for you.

The other mod shop, One-Eyed Willie’s, is more useful. It offers up some really nice off-road options. There aren’t nearly as many off-road modding options in GTA 6 as there are for street cars, so losing out on access to this in the base game is a shame. I also love that One-Eyed Willie’s offers up a random paint job for every car in the game, including non-off-road vehicles, that you can only see once it’s applied. I brought my Banshee into the shop, and it received this pretty pink design that I loved.

The Ultimate Edition also includes some unique free clothing items based on characters from an in-universe cartoon you can watch. These clothes are fine. I guess if you like the show a lot, they might be fun to wear. But…eh.

Beyond the stores and cosmetics, there are some exclusive vehicles you get access to in the Ultimate Edition, but some of these are only available during chapter one for story reasons. The only thing from the Ultimate Edition I used regularly and still use often when I play is the Vapid off-road truck. It’s fast as heck, a great option for driving on the dirt, and can be upgraded into a beast that can hold a lot of stolen loot. There’s also a classic car scavenger hunt side mission hidden behind the paywall, but after 150 hours I’ve barely interacted with that thing.

Answering the big question of “Is the Ultimate Edition worth it?” is tricky, because it depends entirely on what you value and your taste for fashion and cosmetics. I’ve provided some samples of what’s on offer and how it fits into the larger GTA 6 world.

My opinion is that if you can afford the extra $20, a few bits of the Ultimate Edition are nice and worth the upgrade. But for the most part, if you just want to play Grand Theft Auto 6 to enjoy the open world and its story, you don’t need this upgrade. You’ll have a great time with the base game and never think to yourself, “Boy, I wish there were 30 more shirts and a few more cars in this!” GTA 6 is already big. Don’t worry about making it a bit bigger.

There are a lot of new Disney movies that have come out this year, but few are as exciting as Walt Disney Animation’s Hexed. It’s also especially exciting when a release like this means a new character has arrived at Disney Parks. So, that got me wondering: could the new magic-focused movie find a home at one of the resorts permanently? With that in mind, I had to field some early ideas from the movie’s directors when CinemaBlend visited Disney's studio in Burbank, California.

Before we get to that, it should be noted that Billie from Hexed is now meeting guests at Disneyland starting today, and she will be at Hollywood Studios at Walt Disney World starting Wednesday. Check out a first look at how she looks as a Disney Parks character:

A post shared by Disney Parks (@disneyparks)

She looks so good! Disney Parks really got all the details right, making it look like she jumped right out of the new movie. It hasn’t been revealed yet where Billie will be stationed, but I think she would fit right into the upcoming Villains Land. She’s not a villain herself, but she’s from a world of witches, and the vibes just seem to fit. When I shared this idea with the directors of Hexed, one half of the team, Jason Hand, said this:

Villain Land? What about a whole entire land just for Hexe?

OK, now we’re talking! The Hexed trailer shows off a gorgeous new land called Hexe where all witches live. In the new animated movie, Billie opens a secret portal to Hexe after accidentally taking off a bracelet she’s worn all her life that has been concealing her powers. Hexe is a whimsical, beautiful land full of lush forests and magic (of course). Just take a look:

Gorgeous, right? I know I’d especially love to see a recreation of the home of Beef Roger, who is a three-eyed cat who lives on the outskirts of Hexe. Here it is:

I know, I know, perhaps it’s a little too soon to dream up Disney Parks concepts for the movie. It’s not even out yet. But Hexed is getting a ton of positive early reactions for being “unexpected”, and as someone who’s seen the latest from Walt Disney Animation, the studio has definitely created the kind of world I want to visit in real life. Hence, my enthusiasm.

I love how big Jason Hand was thinking regarding how Hexed could fit into Disney Parks, because why not? There’s already a ton of really exciting upcoming Disney attractions on the way, from Monstropolis to Piston Peak; who’s to say Hexed couldn’t become the next. When you check out Hexed, in theaters November 25, you can imagine how you’d like to see it show up in Disney Parks.

#3716. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang accused of decades of bullying and workplace abuse in new investigation

Public humiliation reportedly considered a "rite of passage".

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the company which has long played a major role in PC gaming.

Following Huang's departure, The New York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

The report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, said everyone hoped they'd drop dead.

Huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".

It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's said often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.

A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the New York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, said the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".

Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly said earlier this week that the company "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".
